what_it_does: This paper describes a clock-generation circuit that produces a precise timing reference for high-speed chips at 5.5 gigahertz (GHz) without requiring external quartz crystals. Ring oscillators—circular chains of logic gates where signals loop endlessly—are used as the timing source because they fit compactly on-chip and resist electromagnetic noise. However, ring oscillators are noisy and their frequency drifts with temperature and power-supply voltage. The design uses a feedback-based noise cancellation technique that injects an opposite-phase correcting signal through the power supply to cancel out the main noise component, while a precision converter (time-to-voltage) turns fractional timing corrections into electrical signals to handle quantization noise. The result is a clock with jitter (timing uncertainty) reduced to 290.8 femtoseconds with less than 7.5% degradation across temperature and voltage corners.
